placeholders.label: The Gap
placeholders.description: The missing span of history predating the setting — a Second Impact analogue.

placeholders.label: The six kids and their six Frames
The dig site
placeholders.description: The excavation that produced the Frames and, at the campaign's midpoint, the spaceship. Distinct from "the Gap" (the missing span of history) — this is the physical site.

placeholders.label: The excavated spaceship
placeholders.description: The midpoint-arc ship, unearthed from the same dig site as the Frames, running on the same sync/Resonance technology. Becomes the party's shared asset. See design/campaign-arc.md.

placeholders.label: The school
placeholders.description: Where the kids attend classes. Confirmed as the same combined campus as the Directorate's civil-defense facility (see open-questions.json #school-facility-same-location, resolved) -- this and "the huge facility" from the design bible are one location, so may end up sharing a single name rather than needing two. REFINED 2026-09-12 (LEDGER #13): one campus, one island, but NOT co-sited. The island's north-west end -- causeway, Roadgate, Frame hangar, workshops, vehicle control point, candidate camp -- is "pure military and checkpoints" in Ingram's words; the school is further south-east on the same island. Entry 12's deliberate military/school mix is achieved by walking between the two ends, not by blending them in one place. A single name may therefore still be wrong; check before assuming.

placeholders.label: The Original Cultist
placeholders.description: Working name, 2026-09-13, explicitly not final. The designation for Cicada's unidentified founder. IN-FICTION this is a label for a person nobody has a name for -- the Directorate has never identified him (LEDGER #17), so any term the party or the institution uses is one they invented for a gap in the file. That makes the label itself a piece of characterisation: an institution that gives a case number to someone it cannot name. Whatever this becomes, it must read as something people would actually say out loud in a briefing.

placeholders.label: The Section Officer
placeholders.description: The party's immediate superior and the campaign's in-house petty tyrant (data/npcs/section-officer.json). Needs a name that sounds like a middling rank on a duty roster rather than a villain -- the joke is that he is completely ordinary. Whatever it is, the party will say it a great deal, usually while complaining.
